state.task: Advise how to express the server UI in 20 manually authored JavaScript examples of CanLang’s desired compiled result. Neither a compiler nor imported packages are being built. The human finds existing helper-based rendering too abstract and requests a translation closer to the source, while judging giant HTML strings difficult to read. Preact is one candidate they mentioned; it is not a settled technology choice. Server authority over business records and permissions persists. A separate renewed analysis will assess possible client-side state and rules; selecting a rendering form here should not decide that other question. Until that analysis is resolved, these examples retain the server/HTMX baseline and omit any browser-state implementation.
state.source: The language targets AI-written compact CRUD-oriented business applications on workerd, with a fixed daisyUI/HTMX presentation vocabulary. That vocabulary currently includes page, card, list/table/board, text, details/drawer, edit/action/form, history, metrics, tab, calendar and copy declarations. Preserve page access predicates, present read permissions, containment/record/argument linkage, sorting/search/filters/preference defaults and inline English/Dutch wording. Forms and MCP consume the same owning operation schema. The shared shell, catalog/widget rendering, database reads, permissions, typed formatting, localization and complete-page versus fragment responses are intended imported interfaces whose bodies are absent. The exercise must not add source-language forms or business features.
state.current: Present examples rely on positional functions including card(view,caption,()=>[...]), board(view,model,options,(row,view)=>[...]) and form(view,operation,{arguments:...}). Although explicitly labeled unavailable proposals, they make the source/output correspondence hard for this user to inspect. Examples belong in valid .mjs files next to their .can sources. JSX alone cannot satisfy that file contract without another conversion or changing the artifact; calls to h() and tagged-template expressions require no such JavaScript syntax conversion. The source's token budget need not dictate generated representation length.
state.evidence: The documented Preact h(type,props,...children), also called createElement, constructs virtual nodes (https://preactjs.com/guide/v11/api-reference/). The standalone preact-render-to-string serializer offers synchronous HTML, async rendering and Web Streams paths (https://preactjs.com/guide/v11/server-side-rendering/). Nothing requires browser render/hydrate calls when trees are only serialized on the server to HTML for HTMX. Existing HTM binds a tagged-template syntax to h() and returns trees, instead of concatenating HTML manually (https://github.com/developit/htm). That alternative introduces markup parsing/cache logic and markup-like literals; the latter may share the user's readability concern about long strings. These documents cannot prove workerd support or package cost for the eventual pinned releases; a concrete compatibility build remains necessary later.
state.htmx: According to HTMX's documentation, HTML attributes cause HTTP requests whose normal results are HTML; operation targets and replacements can be stated through hx-post, hx-target and hx-swap (https://htmx.org/docs/). Current server authorization determines access, regardless of HX-Request, which only helps choose presentation. Ordinary/shared interaction still handles focus, other unsaved input, open panels/drawers and error feedback. Those obligations persist with HTMX but do not establish a need for a frontend business store. Element expansion and vnode representation both leave these semantics to the implementation. Do not describe the absent dependencies as working code.
state.alternatives: Server effects, canonical signatures, precise scalars, grants, locales, HTMX interaction and missing shared implementations stay the same in every candidate. Separate two dimensions. For granularity, named catalog nodes with explicit props and children mirror source declarations but conceal their HTML inside standard components. Expanding mostly native HTML with daisyUI/HTMX attributes reveals concrete layout and retains necessary specialized forms/history/collection controls, at the cost of more output and duplicated standard layout detail. Bind collection context through renderRow properties, not callback-valued vnode children. For notation, plain h() needs Preact plus its serializer and can be wordy; short HTM tagged expressions add markup readability and no JSX stage, together with parser/cache code and literals. Both notations support either granularity, so decide independently. Deferral is legitimate if facts or the meaning of closer translation do not justify an option. The proposed example format can be questioned later. Do not build a rendering framework, client app or authored configuration manifest.
state.client_evidence: Browser concerns have distinct kinds: focus/panel/selection/request presentation, unsaved business values in a local draft, caches of authorized stored records, speculative pending record changes, and local evaluation of business logic. Existing journeys require draft retention and explicit in-flight/error feedback. Current CRM stage/results, document revision/reviewer assignment, café conflicts, stock balances and leave coverage depend on current authority. The feedback requirements specifically avoid raising a vote count before confirmation. Canonical field schemas can provide quick native browser validation; the owning server checks complete guards/invariants for every browser or MCP invocation. Advisory pure previews and nonauthoritative caches could improve latency, reuse reads and connect views, provided exact scalar/time representation, permission-safe inputs, cache freshness, concurrent reconciliation and pending/failure feedback are handled. The repo provides no latency/device/cache measurements or source requirement for offline/cross-page transactions that establishes a broad store benefit. Lack of that evidence is not proof that no benefit exists.
state.client_sources: Native constraint checks are defined by the HTML standard (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#the-constraint-validation-api). HTMX offers synchronization, disabled pending controls and element preservation but records text focus/caret limits (https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-sync/, https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-disabled-elt/, https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-preserve/). TanStack distinguishes pending UI-only optimism from modifying caches with cancellation, snapshots, rollback and refetch (https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/optimistic-updates); React describes temporary optimistic values and recovery after actions fail (https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic). They demonstrate available mechanisms and their responsibilities without proving CanLang fit or choosing a package. A single semantic compiler may generate server code plus browser projections/assets from checked CanLang declarations; additional artifacts alone do not imply separate DSL compilers, though extra client behavior requires more checking, protocol and runtime work. Existing bundling or library build steps do not implement CanLang semantics. This task assesses client logic/state and writes no implementation of it.
state.async_scope: Neither async row/guard functions nor Promise values become resolved Preact children merely by entering a vnode tree. Actual source views perform async can_work guards and bind protected rows. A server component therefore needs an explicit authorized bounded-data/renderRow preparation contract or a supported documented asynchronous serializer integration. That outstanding shared obligation affects every representation and does not establish browser-store necessity.

granularity.instructions: Assess the tree’s component granularity separately from its syntax. Balance an inspectable relationship to source with HTML visibility, output size and reuse of standard canonical behavior. Neither component labels nor detailed tags establish correctness. Leave browser-state architecture to its distinct assessment rather than implementing or deciding it through this choice.

criteria.catalog: Build trees from the canonical catalog’s named imported components with explicit properties and nesting. This makes declarations easy to match and preserves shared behavior, but keeps component markup hidden and could remain too abstract for this reader.
criteria.native: Show layout mainly as concrete HTML elements with daisyUI classes and explicit HTMX attributes, retaining needed specialized canonical forms/widgets. This reveals rendering structure, but lengthens output, repeats standard layout and weakens direct source-node correspondence.
criteria.unresolved: Withhold a granularity selection because the user’s interpretation of direct mapping versus abstraction is ambiguous. Prepare a short comparison using a real app section before replacing all UI representations.

notation.instructions: Choose tree notation independently of component expansion, maintaining ordinary .mjs validity. Balance dependency reuse, visible structure and reading cost. HTM returns trees rather than manually joined HTML, yet its markup literal syntax may still be problematic for this user.

criteria.h: Write standard Preact h(type,props,...children) expressions and serialize through its established server package. Benefits are explicit JavaScript with no markup parser or JSX conversion; a deeply nested hierarchy can be verbose and harder to scan.
criteria.htm: Express concise compositional vnode trees with HTM bound to Preact, then serialize on the server. Benefits are markup-like readability without a JSX transform; costs are added parsing/caching and literals resembling the strings the user disliked.
criteria.unresolved: Wait to select h() or HTM because source evidence does not resolve their readability tradeoff. Supply a compact real example in both notations.

client_scope.instructions: Recommend an initial browser-behavior scope for the actual CanLang apps. Compare low-latency feedback, read reuse and cross-view coordination with source compactness, adoption, canonical operation consistency and additional generated/runtime/compiler machinery. Server decisions and browser/MCP equivalence remain mandatory. Reconsider the prior store objection rather than enforcing it as a fixed rule.

criteria.server_baseline: Use server HTML and HTMX with shared drafts, presentation and request/error handling, including native validation derived from field metadata. Initially omit broad stored-record caching and projected business rules. This limits coordination work, but cross-field and record-dependent feedback still waits for requests.
criteria.derived_preview: Provide client-side advisory evaluation of canonical pure rules using only permitted data, including immediate cross-field or exact-total previews, in addition to ordinary local interaction. Keep final server checks and avoid a general record cache. This improves immediate feedback while requiring projection analysis, exact-value support and generated client code.
criteria.hydrated_store: Supply a broad nonauthoritative record cache and optimistic transitions with eligible rules generated from the owning definitions, still invoking the canonical server. This may coordinate views and reduce latency/reads, but demands rollback, freshness/permission invalidation, synchronization and a client-delivery architecture.
criteria.unresolved: Delay the client-scope decision until a concrete UX/latency comparison and cost prototype can assess whether advisory previews or a general browser cache justify their added work.
